Captured 2026-10-22 from the trusted /usr/bin/codex, codex-cli 0.162.0.
No inference turn or provider worker was launched.
The production app-server argv surface (--stdio, --strict-config, all eleven
disabled features, shell-environment controls, project_doc_max_bytes=0 and
the fixed permission profile) also initialized successfully with this binary.

models.json is the projection of `codex debug models` onto slug,
default_reasoning_level and supported_reasoning_levels. Large model prompt
templates and unrelated metadata are deliberately omitted. The capture
advertised nine models, including gpt-reserve and codex-auto-review.

app-server-start.json contains the actual initialize response, disabled
remoteControl/status/changed notification, and thread/start response. The
temporary Codex home/cwd, hostname, installation id and thread/session ids
are normalized. thread/start requested gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh configuration,
on-request/user approvals, ephemeral mode, and the fixed read-only MACO
permission profile. environments=[] was used for this no-turn protocol probe:
a local-environment probe was blocked by this worker sandbox's protected
app-server socket directory. This capture does not qualify tool execution,
containment, authentication, completion, or usage for a live MACO run.

The observed startup notification adds emittedAtMs. That metadata must not
relax envelope, parameter, duplicate-key, remote-control-state or correlation
checks. Thread settings still resolve the exact model, effort, cwd, approval
policy and permission profile using the existing response fields.

R44 round 3 captures, 2026-10-22:

failed-lens-{0,1,2}.jsonl are the entire captured server prefixes from
/home/rikuu/agent-work/maco-e2e-20261015/runs/e2e-mixed-r44a2/repo/.maco/o2/runs/e2e-mixed-r44a2/logs/readme-worker-review-auditor-lens-{0,1,2}.jsonl.
They stopped at account/updated, respectively during inference, before the
thread/start response, and before the turn/start response. Local host/home/cwd
and thread/turn identities are normalized; method order and fields are intact.
The regression replays these original prefixes with a successful capture's
correlated suffix. This stitching is test input, not a claim that the failed
production lenses completed.

auditor-turn.jsonl and worker-turn.jsonl are full inference captures from the
trusted /usr/bin/codex (0.162.0), gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh, through turn/completed.
Both used initialize experimentalApi=true, no opted-out notifications,
ephemeral threads, local environments, on-request/user approval, and the
maco_external_codex permission profile with networking disabled. Apps, plugins,
hooks, browser/computer/image tools, multi_agent, and goals were disabled.
The private homes used a copy of the existing account credentials; credentials
were never captured and were removed after each probe.

The read-only auditor reviewed inline README content without tools. The worker
appended Hello from MACO through native apply_patch to a scratch README in /tmp;
sandbox startup failed and Codex requested approval to retry the patch; the
client accepted that exact scratch-file change with grantRoot=null. The
resulting bytes were independently checked. Neither launched another agent.
These are protocol/inference probes, not end-to-end MACO containment, journal,
acceptance or lens qualification. An earlier shell probe failed at this worker
sandbox's protected app-server socket directory. The worker's outer sandbox
and the configured MACO permission profile were unchanged.

The two full fixtures preserve all server messages, including timing fields,
item lifecycles, account/updated, turn/moderationMetadata,
thread/tokenUsage/updated (including cacheWriteInputTokens), rate limits,
serverRequest/resolved, and terminal events. Host/home/cwd and thread/turn IDs
are normalized; account credit balance is replaced with 1.0000. Token counters,
item IDs, event order, model/effort, request IDs and completion statuses are
unchanged. Tests replay original JSON lines and verify complete parent identity
and exact cumulative input/output/cache/reasoning usage. Missing usage remains
unknown and unsupported methods remain errors.

Additional observed 0.162.0 behavior: turn/started can precede the turn/start
response. A shell probe captured that order; tests move the real lifecycle
notice before its response and require matching IDs, uniqueness and a strict
notification envelope. Only that bounded lifecycle notice is held.

Schema source: `/usr/bin/codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental`.
AccountUpdatedNotification enumerates optional/nullable AuthMode and PlanType;
ServerRequestResolvedNotification requires threadId and requestId. The adapter
checks these shapes from original bytes, rejects unknown/duplicate envelope
and parameter fields, bounds account updates across all phases, and correlates
request resolution with a previously serviced client request.

R44 round 4, 2026-10-22:
failed-worker-journal.jsonl is the complete captured prefix from
runs/e2e-codex-r44a3-1/repo/.maco/o2/runs/e2e-codex-r44a3-1/logs/assignment-001.jsonl.
failed-worker-journal-command.json contains its summary's command array.
Host/workspace/artifact/output/helper paths and thread/turn/installation identities
are normalized. Method order, timestamps, requested settings and approval data
are preserved. The prefix ends at requestApproval: it contains NO completed
command item with the original denial, so the model's read-only-path reason is
not a captured syscall diagnostic. The regression must cancel that request;
it must never turn this prefix into successful execution or acceptance.

The source comparison explaining the missing mount target is:
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.144.4/codex-rs/protocol/src/permissions.rs
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0/codex-rs/protocol/src/permissions.rs
(PROTECTED_METADATA_PATH_NAMES adds .aws), and
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs
(append_metadata_path_masks_for_writable_root, append_missing_read_only_subpath_args).
MACO's carrier already precreated the other three protected targets; the outer
boundary leaves the carrier read-only and mounts only the held journal writable.
The .aws target must likewise be empty, owned, canonical and precreated. This
adds no credential access or writable path. The bound journal's lock is flock
on the existing file, with no separate lock or temporary file.

A real local 0.162.0 sandbox journal probe was attempted in round 4. This Codex
worker session masks /tmp/codex-daemon-1000 as a read-only mode-000 tmpfs.
Codex fails before execution with "app-server socket directory must be a
user-owned directory with mode 0700". That session boundary was not bypassed.
The parent must verify actual sandboxed execution outside this session.

2026-10-29 capacity failure:
thread-system-error.jsonl preserves lines 14-16 of assignment-001.jsonl from
e2e-codex-main-284a-c29a, captured with 0.162.0. Thread/turn IDs are replaced;
all other fields, timestamps and order are preserved. Lens 0 emitted the same
systemError shape followed by serverOverloaded. Each original status frame
was 155 bytes excluding its newline, well below the existing 16 KiB bound.
These are legitimate systemError notifications, not evidence of a protocol
version change. Tests supply a synthetic correlated startup. The variant
without the error notification tests failed terminal handling separately;
it does not claim that the live run succeeded or supplied token usage.
